title: The Spotlight Effect

scenes.vo: That embarrassing thing you did yesterday? Almost nobody noticed.

scenes.text:
Students wore a cringey
Barry Manilow T-shirt
scenes.vo: In a Cornell study, students had to walk into a room full of peers wearing an embarrassing Barry Manilow T-shirt.

scenes.text: They guessed *half* the room would notice
scenes.vo: They guessed about half the room would notice the shirt.
In reality, only about one in four people did.
This is the spotlight effect. We're the centre of our own world, so we assume we're the centre of everyone else's too.

scenes.text:
Everyone's too busy with
*their own* spotlight
scenes.vo: But everyone else is busy worrying about their own spotlight.

scenes.text: Next time you cringe: *halve it*. That's closer to reality.
scenes.vo: So next time you cringe about something, halve it. That's much closer to reality.

scenes.text:
Follow *@inquisitive_bytes*
for a daily byte of behaviour science
scenes.vo: Follow Inquisitive Bytes for a daily byte of behaviour science.

caption: You're not being watched nearly as closely as you think. 🔦 Share this with the friend who's still replaying something from 2019.
source: Gilovich, T., Medvec, V. H. & Savitsky, K. (2000). The spotlight effect in social judgment. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 78(2).
